22. Case study: drug utilisation

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-22-case-drug.Rmd
book-22-case-drug.Rmd

What you will learn

Select a drug class, distinguish stockpiled supply from persistence, and calculate proportion of days covered with an explicit follow-up denominator.

You need: the client packages and the Opal login from Getting started. This chapter uses omop.questionnaire_drugs, then omop.gibleed.

Research question and supply patterns

For new users of a drug class, what fraction of the first year is covered by recorded supply, and when does the first treatment era end? The questionnaire example has three synthetic supply patterns, with 12 people per pattern:

Pattern Fill days from entry Days supplied per fill
Continuous, with early refills 0, 100, 220 120, 120, 125
Two overlapping fills, then stop 0, 30 60, 60
Short course, then restart 0, 120 30, 30

Stockpiling shifts overlapping supply later. For the first pattern, the raw union of fill intervals covers 345 days, but carrying unused supply forward covers 365. A gap over 30 days starts a new era. Predict covered days and first-era duration before examining the summaries.

library(dsOMOPClient)
conns <- ds.omop.login("https://localhost:8443", user = "administrator",
  password = "password", resource = "omop.questionnaire_drugs", server = "site")$conns

Find a class and its descendants 

classes <- ds.omop.concept.search(NULL, vocabulary = "ATC", standard_only = FALSE, conns = conns)$pooled
classes[c("concept_id", "concept_name", "concept_class_id", "standard_concept")]
concept_id concept_name concept_class_id standard_concept
960001 Teaching ATC first level ATC 1st C
960002 Teaching ATC second level ATC 2nd C 
class_id <- classes$concept_id[classes$concept_class_id == "ATC 2nd"]
children <- ds.omop.concept.descendants(class_id, conns = conns)$pooled
children[c("concept_id", "concept_name")]
concept_id concept_name
950001 Questionnaire study medicine 
ds.omop.concept.prevalence("drug_exposure", scope = "pooled", conns = conns)$pooled
concept_id n_persons concept_name
950001 35 Questionnaire study medicine 
class_set <- omop_concept_set(class_id, descendants = TRUE)
saveRDS(class_set, "utilisation-class.rds")

ATC classification concepts have standard status C, so the search includes nonstandard entries. Select second-level class 960002. Its synthetic hierarchy selects 950001, Questionnaire study medicine. The occurrence band 35 means 35–39 exposed people; the analysis below has 36. Class membership comes from the hierarchy, not a drug’s spelling or a Maps to substitution.

Define eligible time and supply

Require a 365-day washout and observed follow-up through day 364: days 0–364 contain 365 eligible days. This complete-follow-up restriction simplifies the denominator but can select people with more stable observation. A different study may instead use variable observed follow-up.

users <- omop_new_users(class_set, washout_days = 365)
drug <- omop_event("drug_exposure", class_set)
era <- omop_era(drug, gap = 30, by = "ingredient", stockpile = TRUE)
covered <- omop_variable(event = era, reducer = omop_reduce("covered_days",
  window = omop_window(0, 364), coverage = "effective_supply"))
persistence <- omop_variable(event = era, reducer = omop_reduce("first_era_days",
  window = omop_window(0, 364)))
study <- omop_study(users, outputs = "baseline", require = list(followup = 364),
  baseline = list(covered = covered, persistence = persistence,
    discontinued = omop_number_flag(persistence, "lt", 365)))
recipe_execute(study, out = c(baseline = "D_supply"), conns = conns)
ds.omop.mutate("D_supply", pdc = covered / 365, newobj = "D_use", conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_use$pdc", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "numeric"
#>
#> $site$length
#> [1] 36
#>
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>        5%       10%       25%       50%       75%       90%       95%      Mean
#> 0.1643836 0.1643836 0.1643836 0.3287671 1.0000000 1.0000000 1.0000000 0.4977169

Mean PDC is 0.4977 across 36 people: (365 + 120 + 60)/(3 × 365). PDC is a dimensionless fraction of eligible days. It measures recorded supply, not ingestion. This class contains one ingredient; a class with several would also need a rule about whether switching preserves persistence.

dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_use$covered",
  datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_use$covered
#>  60 120 365  NA
#>  12  12  12   0

Twelve people each have 60, 120 and 365 covered days, matching the three patterns. The restarted course contributes 60 covered days across two eras, even though its first era lasts only 30 days.

Exercises

1. Compare persistence with coverage. Summarise first-era duration. Explain why it differs from total covered days for the restarted course.

Solution 1

dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_use$persistence",
  datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_use$persistence
#>  30 120 365  NA
#>  12  12  12   0

First eras last 30, 120 and 365 days, with 12 people in each and mean 171.67 days. The gap before the restart exceeds 30 days, so the second course does not extend the first era. A tolerated gap can add to an era’s span without adding covered supply days.

2. Interpret discontinuation. How many first eras end before the first year is complete? Does this prove permanent cessation?

Solution 2

dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_use$discontinued",
  datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_use$discontinued
#>  0  1 NA
#> 12 24  0

There are 24 indicators of one and 12 of zero. The definition says the first era ended before day 365 under this gap rule. It permits restarting, as the third pattern demonstrates; it does not prove permanent cessation.

Check feasibility before applying this to another resource

GiBleed has no ATC hierarchy, but chapter 20 identifies celecoxib ingredient 1118084. Check what its available exposure spans can support.

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
ds.omop.connect(resource = "omop.gibleed", conns = conns)
hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("celecoxib", domain = "Drug", vocabulary = "RxNorm", conns = conns)$pooled
hits[c("concept_id", "concept_name", "standard_concept")]
concept_id concept_name standard_concept
1118088 celecoxib 200 MG Oral Capsule [Celebrex] S
1118084 celecoxib S 
ingredient <- hits$concept_id[trimws(hits$concept_name) == "celecoxib"]

Select the standard celecoxib ingredient by its exact name. An ingredient analysis does not become a class analysis merely by giving it an ATC label.

gibleed_drug <- omop_event("drug_exposure", ingredient)
gibleed_era <- omop_era(gibleed_drug, gap = 30, by = "ingredient", stockpile = TRUE)
feasibility <- omop_study(omop_new_users(ingredient, washout_days = 365),
  outputs = "baseline", require = list(followup = 364), baseline = list(
    covered = omop_variable(event = gibleed_era, reducer = omop_reduce("covered_days",
      window = omop_window(0, 364), coverage = "effective_supply"))))
recipe_execute(feasibility, out = c(baseline = "D_feasibility"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_feasibility$covered", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "integer"
#>
#> $site$length
#> [1] 1745
#>
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>   5%  10%  25%  50%  75%  90%  95% Mean
#>    1    1    1    1    1    1    1    1

Every covered-days summary is one day because the source has zero days supplied and equal exposure start/end dates. These records cannot establish longitudinal adherence or discontinuation, so a PDC conclusion would be unsupported.

Recap

Establish vocabulary and supply-history feasibility, then define follow-up, stockpiling and gaps. Covered days, first-era persistence and discontinuation answer different questions even when derived from the same prescriptions.
